Plans to build four homes at a former kennels and cattery between Hilton and Fenstanton have been refused after a national planning policy change. The application sought permission to demolish the existing buildings at Fields View, Fenstanton Road, Hilton, and replace them with four detached single-storey homes. The scheme had previously been recommended for approval and was backed by councillors in August, subject to a review against a newly published National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF). Plans to build four homes on the site of a former kennels and cattery between Hilton and Fenstanton have been refused after a change in national planning policy prompted Huntingdonshire District Council officers to reverse their earlier recommendation. (Image: HDC) However, planning officers later concluded that the development should be refused after reassessing it under the updated NPPF 2026. Officers told the council's development management committee that the plans would create "isolated homes" in the countryside outside a settlement boundary. rawItems.title: 9 hidden gems in Cambridgeshire you have to visit at least once
rawItems.content: Cambridgeshire is packed with hidden gems that rarely make the county's tourism brochures. From ancient wetlands and secret nature reserves to forgotten archaeological sites and historic country estates, here are nine lesser-known attractions to visit. Often described as a hidden gem, Wicken Fen is the National Trust's oldest nature reserve and one of Europe's most important wetlands. Visitors can explore boardwalks winding through reedbeds, marshes and wildflower meadows while spotting dragonflies, rare birds and grazing Highland cattle. The reserve offers a glimpse into the ancient Fenland landscape that once dominated the region, making it an excellent destination for walkers, families and wildlife enthusiasts. Hidden away between Peterborough and Huntingdon, Holme Fen feels remarkably wild and remote. The reserve is home to the famous Holme Post, marking Britain's lowest land point at around 2.75 metres below sea level. Visitors can explore peaceful woodland trails, wetlands and bird hides while discovering a fascinating story of how drainage transformed the Fens. One of Britain's last remaining washlands, Nene Washes offers spectacular wildlife viewing throughout the year. Winter floods attract thousands of migratory birds, while spring and summer bring breeding cranes, godwits and marsh harriers. Birdwatchers rate it among the county's finest locations, yet it remains surprisingly under the radar with many local visitors. Covering hundreds of acres beside the River Nene

rawItems.title: Residents asked to pick site for new zebra crossing in Huntingdonshire town
rawItems.content: Residents are being asked to help decide where a new zebra crossing should be installed in Ramsey as part of plans to improve pedestrian safety and accessibility in the town. Cambridgeshire County Council is asking residents to choose between two possible sites for the crossing. The proposed locations are: Residents have two sites to choose from one is on High Street, opposite Ramsey Abbey Gatehouse, the other is on Hollow Lane opposite Ramsey Golf and Bowls Club. (Image: Google Maps / Street View) The council said the results of the survey, which runs until midnight on Wednesday, October 28, will be considered alongside other highway, safety and accessibility information before a final decision is made. Residents, students, parents, carers and regular pedestrians are all being encouraged to take part. The council says residents’ views will help identify the safest and most effective site for people travelling on foot. items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Planning Minutes (Agenda - Planning Meeting 24 Sept 2026): Supported planning application 26/00188/FUL for commercial shopfront renovation and heritage signage in the Ramsey Conservation Area.

items.title: Great Whyte Pedestrian Safety & Speed Limit Review
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Minutes (Agenda Full Council 10 September 2026): Council resolved to submit a formal request to Cambridgeshire County Council Highways for a 20mph speed zone and upgraded zebra crossing along Great Whyte, following resident traffic survey feedback.

items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Amenities Committee (Agenda Full Council 10 September 2026): Approved £14,500 contract for drainage improvements across Spinningfield recreation ground, alongside installation of replacement inclusive swing sets in September.
